body: Reason(s) for non-compliance: • The Lead Agency does not always provide a minimum 12-month eligibility period for each child, as required by 98.21(a)(1). (Plan Question 2.5.2a) • The Lead Agency does not appropriately limit what families must report during the 12- month eligibility period to allowable information, as required by 98.21(h)(2). (Plan Question 2.5.4) Overall Target Completion Date: 08/01/2026 Action Step Number Action Step Description Target Completion Date 1 Child care staff will submit White Papers requesting process and automation updates in the Idaho Benefits Eligibility System (IBES) for the following scenarios: -Maintaining a child's eligibility for subsidy for 12 months regardless of their association to an eligible child care provider. -Providing 3 months of Qualifying Activity Protection to continue subsidy eligibility when a family is no longer eligible for/participating with TAFI. -Maintaining a foster child's subsidy eligibility for a full 12 months if the child reunited with their family during their eligibility period. -Ensuring a full 12 months of eligibility for children added to the household once initial eligibility has been determined. These updates will not require policy changes or rule promulgation. 06/30/2025 2 Child care staff will work with Process Engineers and Automation Liaisons to develop updates to the IBES rules engine and benefit process manual and coordinate the timeline for automation development, testing, and implementation of the following scenarios: -Maintaining a child's eligibility for subsidy for 12 months regardless of their association to an 08/01/2026 eligible child care provider. -Providing 3 months of Qualifying Activity Protection to continue subsidy eligibility when a family is no longer eligible for/participating with TAFI. -Maintaining a foster child's subsidy eligibility for a full 12 months if the child reunited with their family during their eligibility period. -Ensuring a full 12 months of eligibility for children added to the household once initial eligibility has been determined. 3 IDHW child care program staff in partnership with the IDHW Legislative and Regulatory Affairs Office will coordinate an update to the Idaho Administrative Code (IDAPA) to limit income reporting requirements after eligibility is determined or reevaluated. Rules will be promulgated for presentation to the legislature's germane committees during the 2026 Idaho Legislative Session. Current notices and processes reflect the reporting income limit of 85% State Median Income, no additional changes will be needed if rules are adopted. 07/01/2026

body: Reason(s) for non-compliance: • The Lead Agency does not limit all family co-payments to seven percent or less of family income, as required by 98.45(l)(3). (Plan Question 3.1.1a). Please note the Lead Agency has an approved waiver for this requirement through August 1, 2026. • The Lead Agency does not provide data on the extent to which CCDF providers charge families additional amounts above the required co-payment (including data on the size and frequency of such amounts), as required by 98.45(b)(5). (Plan Question 3.1.2eii) Overall Target Completion Date: 08/01/2026 Action Step Number Action Step Description Target Completion Date 1 Child care staff will submit a White Paper requesting automation updates in the Idaho Benefits Eligibility System (IBES) to reconfigure the calculation of Idaho Child Care Program (ICCP) copayments capping the total at no more than 7% of the household income. This update will not require policy changes or rule promulgation. 06/30/2025 2 Child care staff will work with Process Engineers and Automation Liaisons to develop updates to the IBES rules engine and benefit process manual and coordinate the timeline for automation development, testing, and implementation of ICCP copayments, capping the total at no more than 7% of the household income. 08/01/2026 3 Child care staff will coordinate with the Self Reliance information/data team to write a report analyzing the extent to which CCDF providers charge families additional amounts above the required co-payment (including data on the size and frequency of such amounts). The report will be published as an appendix to the 2024 Idaho Local Market Rate Report. 12/31/2025

body: Reason(s) for non-compliance: • The Lead Agency does not pay all provider types prospectively or alternatively does not demonstrate that it is not a generally-accepted practice for all provider types, as required by 98.45(m)(1). (Plan Question 4.4.1a). Please note the Lead Agency has an approved waiver for this requirement through August 1, 2026. • The Lead Agency does not pay based on enrollment or alternatively does not provide justification that this is impracticable or is not a generally-accepted practice, as required by 98.45(m)(2). (Plan Question 4.4.1b). Please note the Lead Agency has an approved waiver for this requirement through August 1, 2026. Overall Target Completion Date: 08/01/2026 Action Step Number Action Step Description Target Completion Date 1 Child care staff will submit a White Paper requesting process and automation updates in the Idaho Benefits Eligibility System (IBES) and associated automated financial systems to pay Idaho Child Care Program (ICCP) child care providers prospectively after the first month of eligibility or the first month when services begin, automation updates are not necessary to pay based on enrollment, or the provider's preferred billing practices. These updates will not require policy changes or rule promulgation. 06/30/2025 2 Child care staff will coordinate meetings and seek feedback from child care providers related to prospective payments and enrollment based billing/payments and the best policies and processes to prevent fraud, waste, and abuse. 12/31/2025 3 Child care staff will work with Process Engineers and Automation Liaisons to develop updates to the IBES rules engine and benefit process manual and coordinate the timeline for automation development, testing, and implementation of prospective ICCP after the first month of eligibility or the first month when services begin. System updates do not appear to be necessary to pay based on enrollment, or the provider's preferred payment practices. 08/01/2026 4 Child care staff will coordinate with Child Care Resource Centers and training staff to develop updated information and tools to assist providers with accurate record keeping and timely reporting of ICCP overpayments associate to prospective payments, or payments made based on enrollment after attendance has failed to begin or permanently ceased. 08/01/2026 5 Child care staff will coordinate with the IDWH Central Revenue Unit staff to identify process improvements for reporting and collecting ICCP overpayments associated with prospective payments, or payments made based on 08/01/2026 enrollment after attendance has failed to begin or permanently ceased. 6 Child care staff will work with partners at IdahoSTARS and IDHW Communications Teams to develop a communication plan for child care providers, Child Care Resource Center staff, community partners, and subsidy participating families providing resources and education regarding billing ICCP based on enrollment, allowable charges, temporary and interim ICCP payments, and reporting requirements for providers and families. The ICCP Provider Orientation will also be updated to reflect allowable billing based on enrollment or the provider's preferred billing practices. At this time, these process changes do not appear to require any policy or automation changes as most ICCP participating providers are billing and receiving payments based on enrollment. 08/01/2026

body: Reason(s) for non-compliance: • The Lead Agency's annual monitoring of license exempt in-home care does not meet CCDF requirements as concerns identified during inspections are not cited and enforced, as required by 98.42(b)(2)(iv)(B). (Plan Question 5.5.3a) Overall Target Completion Date: 12/31/2025 Action Step Number Action Step Description Target Completion Date 1 Provider Management Manual Update- Contract managers at Central District Health will develop an updated Provider Management Manual to detail the process for inspecting license exempt in-home child care providers. At this time, we do not believe these updates will require policy changes or rule promulgation. 12/31/2025 2 Communication with Providers- IDHW child care staff, Central District Health staff, and staff at IdahoSTARS will coordinate communication to explain the updates to new and existing in-home child care providers. 12/31/2025 3 Training Inspectors- Contract managers at Central District Health will use the updated Provider Management manual to train and update all child care facility inspectors statewide to conduct inspections of license exempt in-home child care providers. 12/31/2025 4 Contract Update- IDHW child care staff will work with Central District Health staff to amend the contract for inspections and investigations to remove references to "trainings" for license exempt in-home child care providers. 07/01/2025

body: Reason(s) for non-compliance: • The Lead Agency does not sufficiently address the methodology used to complete the narrow cost analysis or estimated cost of care, the variations in analysis, or the assumptions and data included in the methodology, as required by 98.45(f)(1)(ii). (Plan Questions 4.2.2a, 4.2.2b, and 4.2.2c) • The Lead Agency’s payment rates for infants in center-based care, preschoolers in center-based care, and preschoolers in family child care homes are not sufficient to ensure equal access, as required by 98.45(a). (Plan Question 4.3.2a) Overall Target Completion Date: 07/01/2026 Action Step Number Action Step Description Target Completion Date 1 Child care staff will coordinate with the Self Reliance information/data team to add an appendix to the 2024 Local Market Rate study to better address the methodology used to complete the narrow cost analysis and estimated cost of care including the the variations in analysis and 12/31/2025 the assumptions and data included in the methodology. 2 Using the results of the 2024 Local Market Rate study, Idaho Child care staff will work with Automation Liaisons and the Self Reliance Communications team to coordinate updates to the IBES rules engine and Idaho Child Care Program (ICCP) webpage with updated Local Market Rates set at the 65th percentile of the most recent study. Staff will complete automation development, testing, and implementation of the updated Local Market Rates to sufficiently ensure equal access to child care for ICCP participating families. 07/01/2025 3 Child care staff will work with Process Engineers and Automation Liaisons to develop a waitlist for families applying to participate with the Idaho Child Care Program. Processes and automation of a waitlist requires updates to the IBES rules engine and benefit process manual. Automation liaisons and process engineers will coordinate the timeline for automation development, testing, and implementation of an ICCP waitlist. 07/01/2025 4 Child care staff will coordinate review of vulnerable populations not subject to a subsidy waitlist with the Idaho Child Care Advisory Panel. 02/01/2025 5 Once the design is complete, and the process is detailed for the process manual, IDHW leadership will route the processes and policies associated to an ICCP waitlist for legal review to determine if rule promulgation is required for the Idaho Administrative Code or if existing policies fully support the implementation of waitlist. If necessary, IDHW child care program staff in partnership with the IDHW Legislative and Regulatory Affairs Office will coordinate an update to the Idaho Administrative Code (IDAPA) to support the implementation of an ICCP waitlist. If needed, rules will be promulgated for presentation to the legislature's germane committees during the 2026 Idaho Legislative Session. 07/01/2026

body: Reason(s) for non-compliance: • The Lead Agency does not provide grants or contracts for direct services for infants and toddlers, for children in underserved geographic areas, and for children with disabilities, as required by 98.30(b)(1). (Plan Questions 4.1.1c and 4.5.1i). Please note the Lead Agency has an approved waiver for this requirement through August 1, 2026. Overall Target Completion Date: 08/01/2026 Action Step Number Action Step Description Target Completion Date 1 Budget- IDHW leadership will seek legislative approval, and incorporation into the agency's budget, to utilize historically underspent funding to develop contracted child care slots for infants and toddlers, children in underserved geographic areas of Idaho, and for children with disabilities. 07/01/2025 2 Contracts- Child care staff will work with Division Leadership and the Contracts and Procurement team to develop contracted opportunities for child care for infants and toddlers, children in underserved geographic areas of Idaho, and for children with disabilities. Child care staff, Division Leadership, and the Contracts and Procurement team will develop Requests for Information and Requests for Proposals to develop fair and accessible opportunities to provide child care to these populations. 06/30/2026 3 Automation- Child care staff will submit a White Paper requesting automation updates in the Idaho Benefits Eligibility System (IBES) to calculate, determine, and document a child's eligibility for a contracted slot and prevent duplication of eligibility with the Idaho Child Care Program. This update will not require policy changes or rule promulgation. Child care staff will work with Process Engineers and Automation Liaisons to develop updates to the IBES rules engine and benefit process manual and coordinate the timeline for automation development, testing, and implementation of eligibility determinations for contracted slots and prevent duplication of eligibility with the Idaho Child Care Program. 06/30/2026 4 Monitoring- Child care staff will work with the contacts monitoring team to develop tools and resources to ensure financial accountability and 08/01/2026 quality programming for children accessing contracted child care slots. 5 Technical assistance- Child care staff will request, access, and participate with technical assistance related to the development and procurement of contracts for child care for infants and toddlers, children with disabilities, and children in underserved geographic areas because Idaho has never contract for these services before. 12/31/2025

body: Reason(s) for non-compliance: • The Lead Agency does not require an annual unannounced inspection for licensed centers or licensed family child care providers or an annual inspection for license- exempt family child care providers for compliance with a standard for prevention and response to emergencies from food and allergic reactions, as required by 98.42(b)(2)(i)(B). (Plan Questions 5.5.1aii, 5.5.1bii, and 5.5.2bi) Overall Target Completion Date: 10/01/2024 Action Step Number Action Step Description Target Completion Date 1 All health and safety inspectors received an update Child Care Management Manual detailing the policies and procedures for observing and documenting that all licensing and subsidy participating child care providers to have documented procedures for the prevention of and response to emergencies due to food and allergic reactions, and maintenance of records of any medical conditions or allergies that could affect the care of the child and any medications the child is taking or may be allergic to. All health and safety inspections for licensed and subsidy participating child care providers include this criteria. 07/17/2024 2 Idaho Administration Code was updated to require child care providers to have documented procedures for the prevention of and response to emergencies due to food and allergic reactions (16.06.03.380.19). Additional updates require child care providers to maintain records of any medical conditions or allergies that could affect the care of the child and any medications the child is taking or may be allergic to (16.06.03.201.05). 07/01/2024 COMPREHENSIVE BACKGROUND CHECK:5 YEAR RENEWAL Reason(s) for non-compliance: • The Lead Agency does not conduct all background checks every 5 years, as required by 98.43(d)(2)(ii). (Plan Question 5.7.17) Overall Target Completion Date: 12/31/2026 Action Step Number Action Step Description Target Completion Date 1 IDHW child care program staff in partnership with the IDHW Legislative and Regulatory Affairs Office will coordinate an update to the Idaho Administrative Code (IDAPA) to require background checks after 180 days of separation from childcare employment. Rules will be promulgated for presentation to the legislature's germane committees during the 2026 Idaho Legislative Session. 07/01/2026 2 If the legislature approves the requested updates to IDAPA, and sufficient funding is available, IdahoSTARS staff will coordinate automation development associated to individual users the Idaho child care provider database (RISE). The updates will recognize when users have been separated from childcare employment for more than 180 days and flag the necessity of a new background check when new employment is gained. This is targeted for completion six months after the proposed rules would go into effect. 12/31/2026 3 The Lead Agency requires and conducts comprehensive background checks every 5 years. However it was determined that some cities in Idaho who conduct background checks as a component of their licensing programs may not. 06/30/2026 Child care staff will contact each city conducting their own background checks to determine their current areas of compliance, their challenges with meeting the requirements, and identify any areas of concern for elevation to IDHW and city leadership. 4 The Lead Agency requires and conducts comprehensive background checks every 5 years. However it was determined that some cities in Idaho who conduct background checks as a component of their licensing programs may not. Child care staff will identify any areas of concern in city processes and policies and coordinate their review with a focus on solution development with IDHW and city leadership. 12/31/2026 5 The Lead Agency requires and conducts comprehensive background checks every 5 years. However it was determined that some cities in Idaho who conduct background checks as a component of their licensing programs may not. Child care staff will identify any areas of concern in city processes and policies and coordinate their review with a focus on solution development with IDHW and city leadership. 07/01/2027

body: Reason(s) for non-compliance: • The Lead Agency has not established a group size for infants, toddlers, preschoolers, school-age children, or mixed age groups in licensed centers, licensed family child care homes, or license-exempt family child care homes, as required by 98.41(d)(1). (Plan Questions 5.2.2a, 5.2.2c, and 5.2.2d) • The Lead Agency does not require an annual unannounced inspection for licensed centers or licensed family child care providers, or an annual inspection for license- exempt family child care providers for compliance with a group size standard, as required by 98.42(b)(2)(i)(B). (Plan Questions 5.5.1aii, 5.5.1bii, and 5.5.2bi) Overall Target Completion Date: 09/30/2027 Action Step Number Action Step Description Target Completion Date 1 Technical Assistance- Idaho child care staff will participate in requested technical assistance related to the development child care group size limits with a focus on mixed age care, and minimizing the regulatory burden of such a requirement. 12/31/2025 2 Rule Promulgation/Statute Update- Adding a requirement to limit group sizes based on children's ages and development will be a significant undertaking for Idaho, as no similar regulation is currently in place. IDHW child care program staff in partnership with the IDHW Legislative and Regulatory Affairs Office will coordinate an update to the Idaho Administrative Code (IDAPA) and/or Idaho Statute to limit group sizes based on children's ages and development. Due to the complexity of the policy development and coordination, rules and/or statute will be promulgated for presentation to the legislature's germane committees during the 2027 Idaho Legislative Session. 07/01/2027 3 Beneficiary Voice- Idaho child care staff will meet with child care providers throughout the state, ensuring a diverse group of child care providers is coordinated, to seek input and feedback about group size limits that keep children healthy and safe while minimizing the regulatory burden of such a requirement. 06/30/2026 4 Inspections- If the legislature approves the requested updates to IDAPA and/or Idaho Statute, Health District staff will coordinate revisions and updates to the Child Care Provider Management Manual. Health District leadership will train all health and safety inspectors on the approved requirements. 09/30/2027 5 Communication/Outreach- If the legislature approves the requested updates to IDAPA and/or Idaho Statute, Idaho Child Care staff in 09/30/2027 coordination with IdahoSTARS and the Health District will develop tools and resources to communicate the approved requirements to child care providers preparing them to successfully pass their health and safety inspections.

body: Reason(s) for non-compliance: • The Lead Agency does not ensure the privacy of the background check results, as required by 98.43(e)(2). (Plan Question 5.7.10) • The Lead Agency background check agency does not coordinate with other agencies in charge of background checks, as required by 98.43(a)(1). (Plan Question 5.7.11vi) • The Lead Agency does not ensure background checks are completed within 45 days of the request, as required by 98.43(e)(1). (Plan Question 5.7.13a) • The Lead Agency does not ensure that child care staff that reside in a different State receive a comprehensive background check, as required by 98.43(e)(1) and 98.43(a)(1). (Plan Question 5.7.13b) • The Lead Agency does not conduct background checks when a provider is separated from employment for more than 180 consecutive days, as required by 98.43(d)(3)(iii). (Plan Question 5.7.17) Overall Target Completion Date: 07/01/2027 Action Step Number Action Step Description Target Completion Date 1 New Check After 180 Days- IDHW child care program staff in partnership with the IDHW Legislative and Regulatory Affairs Office will coordinate an update to the Idaho Administrative Code (IDAPA) to require background checks after 180 days of separation from childcare employment. Rules will be promulgated for presentation to the legislature's germane committees during the 2026 Idaho Legislative Session. 07/01/2026 2 New Check After 180 Days- If the legislature approves the requested updates to IDAPA, and sufficient funding is available, IdahoSTARS staff will coordinate automation development associated to individual users the Idaho child care provider database (RISE). The updates will recognize when users have been separated from childcare employment for more than 180 days and flag the necessity of a new background check when new employment is gained. This is targeted for completion six months after the proposed rules would go into effect. 12/31/2026 3 Completion within 45 Days- Idaho child care staff will participate in requested technical assistance related to the coordination of completed background checks within 45 days, while still protecting children from potential results delayed by the completion of Child Abuse and Neglect registry checks out of state. 06/30/2026 4 Completion within 45 Days- Child care staff will coordinate with staff from the Idaho Background Check Unit to develop updates to the automated background check system and processes, and coordinate the timeline for automation development, testing, and implementation of the updated background check requirements completing the process within 45 days while still protecting children from potential results delayed by the completion of Child Abuse and Neglect registry checks out of state. 09/30/2027 5 Completion within 45 Days- Adding a requirement to complete background checks within 45 days, 07/01/2027 while coordinating with states other than our own, will be a significant undertaking for Idaho. IDHW child care program staff in partnership with the IDHW Legislative and Regulatory Affairs Office and the Idaho Background Check Unit will coordinate any needed update to the Idaho Administrative Code (IDAPA) to require background check completion within 45 days. Due to the complexity of the policy development and coordination, rules and/or statute will be promulgated for presentation to the legislature's germane committees during the 2027 Idaho Legislative Session. 6 Cities- The Lead Agency ensures the privacy of the background check results, coordinates with other agencies in charge of background checks, and ensures that child care staff that reside in a different State receive a comprehensive background check however it was determined that some cities in Idaho who conduct background checks as a component of their licensing programs may not. Child care staff will contact each city conducting their own background checks to determine their current areas of compliance, their challenges with meeting the requirements, and identify any areas of concern for elevation to IDHW and city leadership. 06/30/2026 7 Cities- The Lead Agency ensures the privacy of the background check results, coordinates with other agencies in charge of background checks, and ensures that child care staff that reside in a different State receive a comprehensive background check however it was determined that some cities in Idaho who conduct background checks as a component of their licensing programs may not. For cities that are not able to demonstrate full compliance with all CCDF background check requirements, IDHW child care staff will coordinate with IdahoSTARS staff and inspectors at the Health District to develop a process to require, and inspect for, a Lead Agency 07/01/2027 background check for providers accessing subsidy. 8 Cities- The Lead Agency ensures the privacy of the background check results, coordinates with other agencies in charge of background checks, and ensures that child care staff that reside in a different State receive a comprehensive background check however it was determined that some cities in Idaho who conduct background checks as a component of their licensing programs may not. Child care staff will identify any areas of concern in city processes and policies and coordinate their review with a focus on solution development with IDHW and city leadership. 12/31/2026

body: Reason(s) for non-compliance: • The Lead Agency does not require and conduct in-state criminal history background checks with fingerprint for all child care staff members (including prospective staff members), as required by 98.43(b)(3)(i), 98.42(b)(2)(i)(B), and 98.43(a). (Plan Questions 5.7.1a and 5.7.1b) • The Lead Agency does not require and conduct in-state criminal history background checks with fingerprints for all individuals age 18 or older who reside in a family child care home, as required by 98.43(b)(3)(i), 98.42(b)(2)(i)(B), and 98.43(a).
